summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was readmitted for acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, likely due to dehydration and reduced oral intake after recent C. difficile infection. She presented with dizziness and fatigue but no falls or respiratory symptoms. IV fluids improved her creatinine from 3.0 to 1.7. Her tacrolimus dose was reduced due to elevated levels and tremor, and metronidazole was discontinued due to gait imbalance. Omeprazole was switched to ranitidine to reduce potential kidney effects. Renal ultrasound suggested right renal artery stenosis, requiring nephrology follow-up. Liver transaminases remained elevated but stable, with no signs of rejection. She was discharged home with home health services, continuing vancomycin for C. diff, and advised to follow up with nephrology, cardiology, and transplant hepatology.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Disorder of bone and cartilage, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Essential and other specified forms of tremor
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
